bib.title: Reproducible scaling laws for contrastive language-image learning

question: How do zero-shot, retrieval, linear-probe and fine-tuning performance of CLIP models scale with model size, data size and samples seen when trained on public LAION data with OpenCLIP?
hypothesis: The pre-training dataset, not the architecture or recipe, explains why OpenCLIP (LAION) and OpenAI CLIP (WIT-400M) show different scaling by task.
contributions: Power-law scaling laws for CLIP across zero-shot classification, retrieval, linear probing and fine-tuning
Evidence that scaling differs between LAION and WIT-400M despite matched architectures and similar recipes
Open release of evaluation workflow and all models including the largest public CLIP models

method.summary: CLIP models (ViT-B/32 to g/14) trained with OpenCLIP from scratch on LAION-80M/400M/2B subsets at 3B/13B/34B samples seen, evaluated downstream. Power laws E = beta*C^alpha are fit on the Pareto frontier of binned total compute (GMAC per sample x samples seen) and compared with OpenAI CLIP models on WIT-400M.
method.task: contrastive language-image pre-training and scaling-law fitting

datasets.name: LAION-2B (English subset of LAION-5B)
datasets.split: full, plus a random 400M subset for a control
datasets.source: Common Crawl, filtered with OpenAI ViT-B/32 similarity

datasets.name: LAION-400M
datasets.source: Common Crawl, filtered with OpenAI ViT-B/32; not a subset of LAION-2B

datasets.name: ImageNet-1k and robustness sets (V2, R, Sketch, ObjectNet, A)
datasets.size: ImageNet test 50,000; V2 10,000; R 30,000; Sketch 50,889; ObjectNet 18,574; A 7,500 (Table 26)

datasets.name: MS-COCO and Flickr30K
datasets.split: test splits from Karpathy and Fei-Fei [36]

datasets.name: ImageNet-12k
datasets.split: subset of ImageNet-22k (14M) for intermediate fine-tuning
datasets.preprocessing: classes with few examples filtered out

models.name: OpenCLIP ViT-B/32
models.architecture: CLIP, ViT image tower 768 width, text 512

other.note: released OpenAI models; ResNets added in Fig 12

training.lr: 1e-3 (global batch ~86-88K), 5e-4 (batch 32K and for H/14, g/14); per run in Table 18
training.lr_schedule: cosine annealing, separate run per samples-seen scale
training.batch_size: global 32,768 to 90,112 (Table 18); 86-88K for most large runs
training.epochs: inferred: 13B samples on 400M data is 32 epochs (Table 12 caption)
training.precision: mixed precision; bfloat16 for L/14, H/14, g/14 after float16 loss spikes
training.hardware: up to 1520 A100 GPUs; JUWELS Booster (A100 40GB) and Stability AI AWS cluster
training.wall_clock: per-run hours in Table 18, e.g. H/14 279 h on 824 GPUs
training.seeds: one trial per config; two trials of B/32 13B gave 63.28 and 63.67

other.data parallel: PyTorch DDP, sharded InfoNCE with differentiable all_gather
other.training sampling: resampling a fixed number of samples per virtual step instead of epochs, 0.1-0.3% difference vs full shuffling
other.gradient fixes tried without success: lower lr, other schedule, gradient clipping, extra norm layers, scaled cosine attention
other.linear probe: Adam, batch 256, sweep lr {0.1,0.01,0.001} x epochs {10,20,40}
other.joint fine-tune on 8 tasks: 2000 iterations, batch 128, lr 1e-5, cosine, 200 warmup, AdamW, wd 0.1, vision encoder only, frozen zero-shot heads
other.ImageNet fine-tune: timm; Tables 10 and 11 list per-size lr, batch, epochs 50/60, layer-wise lr decay, EMA, label smoothing 0.1, stoch depth

inference.prompting: pre-defined prompt templates per class from prior work [55, 84], class embeddings averaged and L2-normalised
inference.retrieval: cosine similarity between image and text embeddings, Recall@5

metrics.name: zero-shot top-1 accuracy
metrics.definition: argmax cosine similarity to averaged L2-normalised prompt embeddings

metrics.name: Recall@5 (image and text retrieval)
metrics.definition: top-5 ranked by cosine similarity on MS-COCO and Flickr30K test splits of [36]; scaling error = 100 - Recall@5

metrics.name: power-law exponent alpha
metrics.definition: fit of E = beta*C^alpha on the Pareto frontier after binning total compute (GMAC per sample x samples seen) and taking the best model per bin

baselines: OpenAI CLIP B/32, B/16, L/14 on WIT-400M
eval.protocol: Fits on few points (low sampling density); control experiments for batch size, 400M subset, trial variance, resampling; pHash duplication check

evidence.quote: global batch sizes in the range of 86-88K samples

results.setup: Zero-shot top-1 ImageNet error vs total compute (GMAC per sample x samples seen), power-law fit on Pareto frontier; OpenCLIP B/32-g/14 on LAION-80M/400M/2B vs OpenAI B/32, B/16, L/14
results.quote: we measure scaling coefficients αopenCLIP = −0.11 and αCLIP = −0.16 for zero-shot top-1 ImageNet

results.claim: Same on the average of five ImageNet robustness sets
results.setup: Average error on ImageNet-V2, R, Sketch, ObjectNet, A; same fit
results.quote: αopenCLIP = −0.13 and αCLIP = −0.24 for ImageNet robustness datasets performance

limits: Sampling density across scales is low, and only 3 OpenAI CLIP models (plus ResNets in Fig 12) are available for comparison since WIT-400M is private
No full hyper-parameter tuning at large scale; control experiments rely on few settings at early stages
Duplication check is a simple pHash test and may miss duplicates
The dataset-composition explanation for the retrieval/classification reversal is a hypothesis that was not tested
Fits give extrapolations only near measured scales; saturation is possible
H/14 and g/14 only measured at one point each (34B and 13B on LAION-2B)
Batch size differs from OpenAI's original recipe (86-88K vs 32K)
